adjudication_label: batch_21:Composition rationale and specific alloy design
canonical_question: Why were Hafnium and Molybdenum specifically chosen over other refractory elements for this specific Ni-rich matrix?

question_variants.question: Why were Hafnium and Molybdenum specifically chosen over other refractory elements for this specific Ni-rich matrix?
question_variants.resolution_summary: Hafnium and Molybdenum were chosen due to their well-known positive effects on mechanical properties of Ni-based superalloys.

answers.answer: Hafnium and Molybdenum were added in small amounts (0.5 and 1.0 at.% respectively) because of their well-known positive effects on mechanical properties of Ni-based superalloys.
answers.material: Al 10 Co 25 Cr 8 Fe 15 Ni 36 Ti 6 with Hf and Mo additions
answers.measurement_outcome: added in small amounts (0.5 and 1.0 at.% respectively)
answers.mechanism: well-known positive effects on mechanical properties of Ni-based superalloys
evidence_spans: The alloy Al 10 Co 25 Cr 8 Fe 15 Ni 36 Ti 6 exhibited a dendritic microstructure after the casting process.
Subsequent annealing for 50 h at 900 °C lead to a three-phase microstructure
Figure 1 a) shows the large (several 10 µm), randomly distributed Heusler type phase, with its characteristic needle-like shape and a volume-fraction of <5%.
